profile.bio: I build backend systems and AI products that hold up in the real world: Go and Python services, event-driven workers, agent harnesses and retrieval, with cost and reliability designed in.

featured.name: Hireish
featured.tagline: An AI interviewer for technical hiring.
featured.description: One link runs the interview loop. Hireish conducts live voice, coding and system design rounds, asks real follow-ups, scores six dimensions as it goes, and produces an evidence-backed report the moment the interview ends.
featured.problem: Technical hiring is slow and inconsistent. First-round screens burn senior engineers' time, five interviewers apply five different bars, and decisions rest on gut feel with no shared evidence trail.
featured.solution: A live AI interviewer that runs the round end to end. It conducts voice interviews over the OpenAI Realtime API, runs coding in a sandboxed editor and system design on a diagram canvas, scores each answer against a configurable rubric, runs anti-cheat in the background, and ships a PDF report with verbatim quotes and a hiring recommendation.

decisions.title: Go for the edge, Python for the AI
decisions.body: High-throughput API and gateway work lives in Go. Interview orchestration and ML integration live in Python, where the tooling is. Each service deploys independently.

decisions.title: Coding and design as first-class rounds
decisions.body: Candidates write code in a Monaco editor backed by a sandboxed Judge0 runtime and sketch architectures on a React Flow canvas, so the interviewer can probe real work instead of recitations.

decisions.title: Anti-cheat as a pipeline, not a checkbox
decisions.body: Face and head-pose detection with MediaPipe, keystroke confidence scoring, prompt-injection filtering, and a WebSocket observer mode that lets a committee watch live.

decisions.title: Model routing per workload
decisions.body: Realtime voice moved to a mini realtime model and the evaluation LLM to a smaller model, with per-organisation model selection so quality and cost are a setting, not a rewrite.

decisions.title: Spend fewer tokens before spending fewer dollars
decisions.body: A client-side energy gate drops silent audio before it is sent, transcript checks avoid full responses to filler, and the system prompt was trimmed from about 3,500 to about 1,800 characters.

decisions.title: Cache what repeats
decisions.body: Relevance filtering, embeddings and confidence scoring are cached on SHA-256 keys with TTLs, so identical work skips the LLM call entirely.

decisions.title: Measure per interview
decisions.body: Token and audio usage are recorded per interview with an estimated cost, exposed through a cost breakdown API.

tradeoffs: Smaller models cut cost sharply but give up some depth; the premium realtime model stays available per organisation.
Six microservices isolate concerns and scale independently, at the price of more deployment and observability surface.
Audio gating saves tokens but a threshold that is too aggressive could clip quiet speakers, so it is tuned conservatively.
outcomes: Projected LLM cost per interview hour fell from about $4.14 to about $0.70 (about 83%) across the documented optimisation phases. This is a projection from the cost model, not measured billing.
Interview reports include six scored dimensions, verbatim quotes and a Strong yes to No recommendation.

faq.a: Hireish is an AI interviewer for technical hiring, live at hireish.in. It runs voice, coding and system design rounds, asks follow-ups, scores six dimensions live and produces an evidence-backed report. Abhishek built it as six Go and Python microservices with a React 19 front end, OpenAI Realtime for voice, a Judge0 sandbox for code and MediaPipe-based anti-cheat.

Hireish (a multi-service AI interview platform), distributed Go backend systems with a worker-consumer architecture at Orange Health Labs, Jarvis (an AI code-intelligence platform with 8+ agents), Zest (an AI ticket triage tool), and side projects like SBANetwork and AllOne.

faq.q: What AI systems have you built?
faq.a: At Orange Health Labs: Jarvis, a code-intelligence platform indexing 63 repositories with a vectorless hybrid RAG pipeline (tree-sitter, dependency graphs, BM25, FTS5) that raised answer accuracy from about 55% to about 90%, with 8+ agents on top (JIRA-to-PR, RCA investigator, PR reviewer, SQL agent); and Zest, which triages Freshdesk tickets and drafts replies with an LLM. Outside work: Hireish.

faq.q: How do you reduce AI costs?
faq.a: On Hireish the levers were model routing (smaller models for realtime and evaluation, selectable per organisation), dropping silent audio before it is sent, trimming the system prompt, caching repeated LLM and embedding calls on SHA-256 keys, and tracking cost per interview. The documented projection is roughly $4.14 down to $0.70 per interview hour.

SBANetwork is a lightweight, CPU-based neural network library inspired by Keras, published on PyPI (pypi.org/project/sbanetwork) under the MIT licence. It has Dense and Dropout layers, six optimizers, fourteen activation functions and five loss functions.
AllOne is a secure password manager with a TOTP authenticator and AI-powered document search, available at allone.co.in.

Abhishek is an SDE-1 at Orange Health Labs in Bangalore (since May 2026; Associate Software Engineer Aug 2025 to Apr 2026). He designed distributed Go backend systems for lab operations, built event-driven pipelines and a worker-consumer architecture on Redis and Memcache, cut report generation latency, and migrated reporting from Jinja2 to Marko.js.
